chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Haytham al-Ajali told us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan told us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib told us, saying: Abu Muhammad Tamim ibn Buhlul told us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them.

He said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, was sitting on a day, and with him were Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn, peace be upon them. Then he said: By He who sent me with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, there is no creation on the face of the earth more beloved to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, nor more honored for Him than us. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, derived for me a name from His Names, so He is al-Mahmud (the Praised) and I am Muhammad. He derived for you, O Ali, a name from His Names, so He is al-Aliyy al-A'la (the High, the Most Sublime) and you are Ali. He derived for you, O Hasan, a name from His Names, so He is al-Muhsin (the Beneficent) and you are Hasan. He derived for you, O Husayn, a name from His Names, so He is Dhu al-Ilhsan (the One of Good Deeds) and you are Husayn. He derived for you, O Fatima, a name from His Names, so He is al-Fatir (the Splitter/Originator) and you are Fatima. Then he, peace be upon him and his family, said: O Allah, I bear You as witness that I am at peace with those who are at peace with them, at war with those who are at war with them, a lover of those who love them, a hater of those who hate them, an enemy of those who antagonize them, and an ally of those who befriend them, because they are from me and I am from them.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The People of the House (Family of the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: How are the names of the Ahl al-Bayt derived from Allah's Names according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar* articulates the Shia doctrine of *Isma* (divine naming) by linking the Ahl al-Bayt’s identities directly to Allah’s attributes, such as 'Al-Fatir' for Fatima and 'Al-Husn' for Hasan. It underscores their ontological closeness to the Divine, serving as a foundational text for understanding their spiritual authority and the covenant of love (*Mawaddah*) required of believers. The Prophet’s concluding prayer emphasizes that loyalty to them is inseparable from loyalty to him, reinforcing their role as the true successors of prophethood.
